Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

scphasedcn (development version)

  • Tumour mode fits the clone baseline (ploidy) by default (clone_defaults() ploidy = "fit"). Up to now the median depth of every clone was taken to be 2 copies, so a near-triploid or whole-genome-doubled clone got states on a compressed scale: 2:2 as 1:1, 2:0 as 1:0, 3:0 as 2:0, and depth-neutral 2:1 often as 1:1. fit_clone_states(baseline = "fit") now fits per clone the copy number of its median depth (the baseline: 1.5 to 5) from depth and alleles together, so states are absolute copy numbers.

    • The fit compares baselines on one likelihood scale. Above a baseline of 2 the state grid drops the near-balanced states such as 4:3, which would only absorb orientation bias.
    • A clone whose allele attenuation is at the grid floor carries no allelic information on the scale. It takes 2 or the sample baseline (the cell-weighted median of the informative clones).
    • Half the best baseline is preferred within ploidy_tol, because a whole-genome doubling of the same profile fits equally well.
    • Labels stay relative to the diploid normal: 2:1 is a gain at any baseline, 1:1 neutral.
    • clones gains baseline and ploidy (the mean autosomal copy number), and the run notes list the baselines.
    • A clone fitted at baseline 2 has exactly the states of 0.1.x. ploidy = 2 restores the old behaviour for every clone; a number fixes the baseline.
    • On COLO829 (bulk ploidy 3.1) the clones fit baseline 3 (one small clone 2.75 in a joint tumour + normal run). A near-diploid tumour stayed at 2 at three seeds, with results identical to those without the fit.

  • Normal mode: windowed, orientation-free allele term (window_allelic_features(), caller_defaults() win_*). With chromosome-scale (hybrid) phasing the per-cell allele term summed oriented votes over the whole region, so an LOH carried by one cell only was cancelled at population-phase switches: a cell with several whole-chromosome losses and CN-LOH could go uncalled and even become a null cell. cell_features() now also sums, per cell and region, the mirrored beta-binomial LLR of near-complete LOH (f = 0.98) over 1 Mb windows x phase sets, with the phase trusted only inside a window. These are the new feature columns wal_f980 and n_win. Windows with a shared allelic bias over all cells are left out, and only autosomes are scored.

    • caller_normal() scores the per-cell loss / CN-LOH rows with the better of the oriented and the windowed LLR where the windowed LLR is above win_min (15) (win_score = "max", under the same cross-validated thresholds). Gains and pooled scores are unchanged.
    • select_null_cells() never takes a cell whose windowed LLR on a chromosome or arm row exceeds the exp(-t) bound at the selection quantile (about 9.2; null_win_guard).
    • How the windowed calls are controlled. The guard bound is below win_min. The windowed term therefore never raises a chromosome or arm row of a selected null cell, and the null false-call rates per 1,000 are those of the oriented scores: they cannot show false calls of the windowed term. Those calls are controlled by win_min and the model bound P(W > 15) <= 3e-7 per row. The selection-free null check (call_scn(null_check = TRUE)) counts them.
    • On a normal thyroid sample (4,105 cells), 2 of 4.0 million cell-region rows have W > 15 (two 5-10 Mb tiles, none on a chromosome or arm; 5 and 10 Mb tiles are not called per cell). The cell calls number 132 rows, as without the term, and the null rates and the null check stay where they were (1.62 / 1.78 per 1,000, chromosome / arm rows).
    • On a COLO829BL (lymphoblastoid) sample with hybrid phasing, a cell with monosomies 1/3/9/12/21 and CN-LOH 8/18 now gets exactly those calls. Of 484 LOH calls, 429 (89 %) lie on ASCAT.sc-HP LOH segments.
      • The null false-call rates stay at about 1 per 1,000.
      • The selection-free null check rises from 2.16 to 2.77 (chromosome rows) and from 2.88 to 3.30 (arm rows). This comes from window-supported LOH rows of cells selected on the other half of the autosomes (85 of 112 on ASCAT.sc-HP LOH segments). Exceedances without window support do not rise (230 -> 221).
      • The guard takes 111 cells out of the null set, which also makes the depth null tighter: +39 depth-only rows, mostly male chrX (69 -> 105 chrX rows).
    • Under block-only phasing the term is not computed (noted), and features computed before this version run as before.
    • New simulator event type "nucleus:<i>", which puts several events in one nucleus.

  • Tumour mode, gain_support (segment_clone(), clone_defaults()): an imbalanced gain state needs depth support against the region’s offset in the other clones. A run without it becomes CN-LOH when its allelic excess supports that, otherwise it keeps its state with label imbalance and a new depth_ok column FALSE. MEDICC2 input treats such runs as 1:1. It addresses clones that mix LOH and heterozygous cells being fitted with false gain states (issue #4).

  • Tumour-mode defaults changed to coarse, reproducible clones. disc_allele = "fraction", test_allele = "centred", drift_test = "modes_event", same_post = "group" and gain_support = 0.3 are now the defaults of clone_defaults() and caller.yaml. On the lab’s tumour benchmarks this gives fewer clones and doublet clones and much better seed agreement. Allele-only subclones smaller than the cell-level haplotype drift are merged. Set the five options back to "z", "z", "none", "clone" and 0 for the behaviour of 0.1.1. Normal mode is unchanged.

  • New single-cell track plots. cell_tracks() builds, for each cell, the depth log2 ratio (1 Mb and aggregated windows, on the scale of the clone segments) and the phased B-allele fraction (phase blocks oriented leave-one-out by the cell’s clone pseudobulk in tumour mode), together with the fitted segments: the clone’s segments, inherited or confirmed in the cell, or the cell’s own events in normal mode. plot_cell_tracks() plots one cell and plot_cells_pdf() writes many cells to a multi-page PDF. ggplot2 and patchwork are suggested packages, and ggrastr is used when installed.

  • inst/scripts/plot_cells.R: command-line front end that plots every cell of a caller run, one PDF per clone (or per stratum in normal mode). It recomputes the feature step when no features .rds is given.

  • Tumour mode with a fitted baseline, details and known limits:

    • Per-cell confirmation scores every null row relative to the neutral state of its own cell’s clone (its baseline and its depth contrast c), so a diploid reference cell is not scored as a one-copy gain of a near-triploid clone. A piece without a state of a clone is taken at that clone’s baseline.
    • Without a reference pool, the neutral of a haploid row (male chrX / chrY) is one copy. A haploid gain could not be confirmed by depth before. This changes calls on those rows in tumour runs without a reference pool, also at the diploid baseline.
    • Baseline candidates are narrowed only after a fit in which at least one clone carried allelic information.
    • ploidy is “fit” or a number in [1, 8], also from a config file.
    • A clone whose depth contrast c is at the lower bound of its grid (0.6) has a poorly determined scale and can be off by one copy; the run notes name such clones. Baselines 0.25 apart are near-ties when c is free.
    • Labels stay relative to the diploid normal, so per-cell call counts rise for clones with a baseline above 2. On a whole-genome-doubled tumour the false confirmations on control pieces stayed below 1 per 1,000 on average, with one small clone at 3 per 1,000.
    • With an odd baseline, a region without allele votes (a female chrX is excluded from the allele channel by default) can only take a balanced state, one copy off the baseline.
    • In simulations at four seeds the fit put a clone at a quarter-step baseline next to the true one (2.25 for 2, 2.75 for 3) in 3 of 12 tumour runs; in one of them a 2:1 chromosome of a diploid clone came out as 3:1. ploidy = 2 avoids this for tumours known to be near-diploid.

  • Tumour mode memory and run time: the per-cell confirmation and the reference cleaning build their vote tables per clone, the matched null is scored one hypothesis at a time, and the baseline fit’s segment refinement no longer recomputes the allele terms per depth contrast. Results are unchanged. On a whole-genome-doubled tumour of about 10,000 cells the fitted baseline needs less memory than the same run needed before the baseline fit (34 GiB against 42 GiB).

  • Tumour mode without flagged null cells no longer fits its input depth t null and allelic rho on all cells. It fits them on the cells without a call on the null rows (new tumour_null_fit()) when that selection is stable, and falls back to all cells otherwise. The run warns, the run notes record which null was used, and the warning also says when the selection keeps more than two thirds of the cells: a stable selection does not show that the cells are copy-number neutral. Results change for such runs; runs with flagged null cells give the same calls.

    • call_scn(mode = "tumour", null_cells = "select") selects the cells for the input null instead of being ignored, and no longer warns that “the features carry their own null fit” when it has just fitted that null.
    • Without an input rho, caller_tumour() and the MEDICC2 helpers use tumour_null_fit() with the caller’s parameters and without multiplets, instead of a rho on all null rows of the flagged cells.

  • Calls require a positive score, score > max(thr, 0), in every comparison of a score with its null threshold: per-cell calls, pooled calls, tumour confirmation, null-cell selection, the null check, event_fdr() and the reference-pool cleaning. Results change only where a null threshold is negative (vote-rich classes, the opt-in confirm_sided = "one"). The thresholds tables still report the null quantile itself.

  • Pooled thresholds are computed for fold 0 only: thresholds.tsv no longer has pooled fold 1-4 rows, and the pooled step is several times faster. Calls are unchanged.

  • Normal mode, opt-in attenuation-aware state set for chromosome-scale phase sets: states_normal is "normal" (default, unchanged), "normal_att" (loss and CN-LOH also scored over f_att_normal, default 0.70-0.98; 1 - eps is always included) or "auto" (normal_att when the phasing regime is chromosome). Calls carry f_state, the best-fitting fraction of the called state. With the windowed allele term only the rows at 1 - eps take the windowed LLR. It trades recall of attenuated losses and CN-LOH against more false loss / CN-LOH labels and some gain recall; in the author’s benchmarks no attenuated grid kept false arm losses within the target, so it is not the default.

  • model depth normalisation, opt-in gc_method = "ratio": the per-cell GC trend from summed counts over GC quantile groups instead of a lowess of per-bin log ratios, which adds a depth-dependent GC bias at low depth. It is applied when features are built, so existing feature files must be recomputed. The default "lowess" is unchanged.

  • Normal mode fixes:

    • A named event in a depth stratum without a depth-null fit of its sd_class takes that sd_class’s fit over strata; before, it got no depth null and was never called. Events of different sizes in one stratum each use their own sd_class fit.
    • select_null_cells(): a class x stratum whose cells were all dropped is thresholded at class level, and a cell with a row that cannot be thresholded is not selected; before, such cells could re-enter the null set. It returns an empty set instead of an error when every candidate is guarded or called.
    • A cross-validation fold whose threshold is NA (empty training set) uses the fold-0 threshold.
    • caller_normal(): cells without a cell type in cell_meta keep the features’ cell type.
    • make_pools() and chrom_rank() order names in C order, so a seed gives the same pools under any collation, also for non-ASCII names.
    • caller_normal(), select_null_cells(), pooled_thresholds() and null_selection_check() complete a partial params list with caller_defaults().
    • win_allelic values other than TRUE / FALSE / “auto” stop with an error; pool_scale() default tail_k is 30, as caller_defaults(); subset_scn() keeps the requested order for integer selectors and stops on duplicate or unknown cells; make_cell_meta() warns when qc_args are not applied.
    • Missing categorical values in h5ad obs / var tables are read as NA in place, no longer shifting later values.

  • Tumour mode fixes:

    • Each EM round removes only its own doublet clones (ids were kept across the renumbering of the split pass), so clones has unique ids and every doublet flag is in null_fit$clones$doublet_log. Doublet clones flagged in the global round no longer appear as clones rows.
    • caller_tumour() accepts every multiplet form of multiplet_table() and stops clearly when allelic_exclude leaves no allele votes.
    • segment_clone(gain_support): a gain is above the clone’s integer baseline and a run is never replaced by its own state. split_disagree() tests clones on the state grid of their baseline.
    • Documented that the confirmation null refits rho only, never the depth t.

  • MEDICC2 export:

    • No segment spans a dropped range (medicc2_pieces(max_gap = 0) by default; medicc2_table() never merges across gaps).
    • Per-cell states keep the chaining flip in the leave-one-out orientation: cells of the reference clone were scored on the wrong haplotype on flipped pieces.
    • imbalance segments enter at the least-imbalanced state of the clone’s integer baseline; medicc2_table() warns when it clips at cap; cell_piece_states(baseline = ) scores cells of clones with a baseline other than 2; numeric clone ids are handled.

  • Functions that seed the random-number generator restore the caller’s random state (normal mode, tumour mode and the simulator’s genome). Results of call_scn() are unchanged; a script that draws random numbers after calling one of these functions directly sees another stream.

  • The caller finds the extractor’s bins file under its bin-size name (bins_<tag>.h5ad) through the new bins_file(); bins_100kb.h5ad is still preferred when present. Bin sizes other than 100 kb are readable but not validated.

  • Single-cell track plots: the depth baseline follows the features’ depth reference and the clone’s ploidy baseline, normal-mode events on haploid chromosomes get haploid states, a clone’s reportable segments that the cell does not confirm are drawn as inherited, and every state label has a colour.

  • Follow-up fixes:

    • clean_reference(): when no clone has allele votes on its event or control regions, the whole candidate pool is kept (threshold Inf) instead of an error.
    • caller_tumour() checkpoint: a resumed run continues with the candidate baselines (and run notes) of the run that wrote the checkpoint, so it gives the same results.
    • simulate_scn(): a genome expression that draws random numbers no longer moves the caller’s random stream.
    • assign_cells(): a piece without a state of a clone on a haploid chromosome is scored as the neutral 1:0 (it was taken at the clone’s baseline, i.e. at the cell’s median depth).
    • Tumour mode takes the depth as relative to the reference pool whenever there is one; with a min_ref below 10 the assignment and the per-cell scores ignored a pool of fewer than 10 cells that the clone profiles used.
    • cell_tracks(): in tumour mode the depth baseline follows the caller’s (B copies without a reference pool, whatever the features’ depth method).
    • cell_tracks(): a segment is drawn as confirmed only when its call is reportable, so the confirmed segments are the cell’s events.
    • plot_cells_pdf() falls back to pdf() when cairo_pdf() opens no device (macOS without XQuartz), and restores the device that was current; raster = TRUE draws unrasterised points, with a message, where ggrastr cannot rasterise.

  • Simulator:

    • simulate_scn(): seed now controls the simulated data when the genome is the default or an inline sim_genome(); before, every seed gave the same data. Seed 1 with the default genome gives the same data as before. With a genome table built beforehand (g = sim_genome(); simulate_scn(genome = g)) or a user’s own bins table, the simulated data differ from earlier versions at every seed, because the random stream now starts after the genome’s draws.
    • Het SNPs are at unique positions; a draw on an occupied position moves to the next free one.
    • write_bins_h5ad() / write_alleles_h5ad(): missing values in character columns are written as anndata categoricals and read back as NA, instead of as the string "NA".

  • Tests: the main normal-mode and tumour-mode simulations are also checked at three further seeds. Before the seed fix every simulated fixture was drawn from one random stream, whatever seed it named.

  • Extractor (Python):

    • extract / run check each chromosome against the BAM header, the FASTA and the chromosome sizes before the BAM pass. A mismatch (another assembly or naming) stops with a message naming the file, instead of binning on the wrong lengths or writing bins without GC.
    • QC-fail reads (flag 0x200) are skipped and counted in a new n_qcfail column. Primary records without CIGAR are skipped (they crashed the chromosome) and counted in n_no_cigar; they are not in the per-cell record counts. Records without SEQ count in depth and fragments but carry no SNP observation (counted in n_no_seq).
    • FRiP (frip) counts peak fragments among the clean (non-blacklisted) fragments, matching its denominator; values drop slightly where blacklisted fragments overlap peaks.
    • Biallelic SNVs require REF and ALT in A/C/G/T everywhere (extract, select-hets, hybrid-phase). A SNP inside a reference skip of a read is no longer counted as an other allele.
    • The bins file is named after the bin size by default (bins_100kb.h5ad for 100 kb as before); --tag still overrides.
    • merge without --chroms merges the chromosomes run extracts (the main chromosomes of the BAM header) and fails, naming them, when some have no finished partial (a job that died); --allow-missing merges without them and lists them in summary.json. Without an output directory it gives a usage error.
    • merge removes any other bins_*.h5ad of the output directory, so a re-run at another bin size leaves one bins file.
    • index-check exits with status 1 on a stale or missing index.
    • run reports a worker killed for memory with the unfinished chromosomes and a hint to lower --jobs, and removes the finished-markers of the chromosomes it extracts before starting, so only chromosomes finished in that run count as finished.
    • select-hets --loci matches loci contigs that differ by the chr prefix. select-hets fails when no site is selected (it wrote an empty VCF) and warns when none is on an autosome.
    • A FASTA without chrM, or with another chrM length, is a warning: chrM’s bins have no GC content.
    • The bins file tag of a depth layer written by an older version follows that layer’s own bin size.
    • The per-bin layers are built sparse, with identical output and far less memory at small bin sizes.
    • Since 0.1.1: --vote-ps (one vote per phase set), input metadata in each partial with checks at merge, --allow-missing, an interruption-safe merge, and a report of barcode-map matches.

  • Development versions are marked as such (R 0.1.1.9000, Python 0.1.2.dev0), and the extractor records its version in its output. Python packaging uses an SPDX license expression and needs setuptools >= 77.

scphasedcn 0.1.1

  • Extractor (Python): the read_id of a read whose name does not follow the SPLONGGET convention (<CB>_#<uuid>_<sign><piece>of<npieces>) is now a stable 64-bit blake2b digest of the name. It was Python’s hash(), which is salted per process, so for BAMs from other pipelines the read_id column of fragments.tsv.gz changed from run to run. Reads named in the SPLONGGET convention are unaffected, and so are depth, alleles and the caller.
  • No changes to the R package.

scphasedcn 0.1.0

First public release of scphasedcn.

  • call_scn(): copy-number calls per cell and region from an extraction directory (scphasedcn run), combining read depth and read-phased alleles.
    • Normal-tissue mode (caller_normal()): null cells selected from the data, Student-t / beta-binomial nulls, fold-cross-validated thresholds at 1 false call per 1,000 null cell-regions, per-cell and pooled calls, events.
    • Tumour mode (caller_tumour()): clone discovery, allele-specific clone copy-number states, likelihood assignment of every cell, per-cell inherited and confirmed calls, MEDICC2 input (medicc2_pieces(), medicc2_table()).
  • write_scphasedcn() / read_scphasedcn(): flat result tables, the parameters used (params.yaml) and run notes.
  • Command line: system.file("scripts", "call_scn.R", package = "scphasedcn"), on --dir + --out, or on a sample yaml (inst/extdata/sample_template.yaml) with --config + --sample.
  • make_cell_meta(): the cell metadata table (cell types, known copy-number-flat cells, groups) from the extractor’s cells_qc.tsv and your own labels.
  • The hg38 centromere table ships with the package (hg38_centromeres()); the chrX centromere is masked like the autosomal ones.
  • simulate_scn() / write_sim_dataset(): simulated SPLONGGET-like data in the extractor’s layout.
  • Vignettes: getting started, inputs (phasing recipe, extraction, cell metadata), outputs.
